episodes.title: Heaven's Gate Still Answers Emails
episodes.description:
The Heaven’s Gate website from 1997 is still online and still being maintained. People who contact it have reported receiving replies from individuals who say they are “staying behind” to share the group’s beliefs.

In March 1997, 39 members of Heaven’s Gate were found dead in a mansion in California. They had recorded farewell videos, packed identical bags, and believed they were about to leave Earth aboard a spacecraft following the Hale-Bopp comet.

Heaven’s Gate was a sci-fi oriented religious group led by Marshall Applewhite, who taught that humans could advance a higher, non-human form. Members gave up their identities, families, and possessions in preparation for what they called “the Next Level.”

Nearly three decades later, the group’s original website remains active, using the same design and language it had in the 1990s.

This video looks at how the group formed, what they believed, what led to the deaths of its members, and why their website is still online today.

episodes.title: A Cult, a Terror Attack… and This Video Game
episodes.description:
A Japanese cult, a real terror attack, and a strange piece of media that followed.

In 1995, Aum Shinrikyo carried out the Tokyo subway sarin attack, one of the deadliest acts of domestic terrorism in modern Japanese history. In the years surrounding the attack, the group produced a range of unusual media, including propaganda, music, and video content.

One of the most obscure is a little-known PC title often referred to as The Story of Kamikuishiki Village, often described online as an “Aum cult video game”.

But what actually is it? Was it made by the cult itself, or is the story more complicated?

This video breaks down what we know, what has been misreported, and why this strange artefact continues to circulate decades later.
